<div class="gallery-card">
<a href="gallery/spectral_pde.qmd">
<img class="gallery-card-img" src="Figure/heat_diffusion.gif" alt="Heat conduction solved with the FFT">
<div class="gallery-card-body">
<div class="gallery-card-title">Heat Conduction with the FFT</div>
<p class="gallery-card-desc">In Fourier space the Laplacian becomes −k², so the heat equation turns into one exponentially-decaying ODE per mode — solved exactly, with no time-stepping.</p>
<span class="gallery-card-tag">Ch.4 · Spectral Method</span>
</div>
</a>
</div>

<div class="gallery-card">
<a href="gallery/spectral_em.qmd">
<img class="gallery-card-img" src="Figure/unit_pulse.gif" alt="Electromagnetic waves solved with the FFT">
<div class="gallery-card-body">
<div class="gallery-card-title">Electromagnetic Waves with the FFT</div>
<p class="gallery-card-desc">The same trick for light: the curl becomes i·k×, and each mode oscillates at ω=ck. Spectral solvers (PSTD/PSATD) keep the wavefront on the light-cone where finite differences ripple.</p>
<span class="gallery-card-tag">Ch.4 · Spectral Method</span>
</div>
</a>
</div>

<div class="gallery-card">
<a href="gallery/fft_multiplication.qmd">

<div class="gallery-card-body">
<div class="gallery-card-title">Fast Multiplication with the FFT</div>
<p class="gallery-card-desc">Multiplying two numbers is convolving their digits — so the convolution theorem multiplies million-digit integers and polynomials in O(n log n) instead of O(n²).</p>
<span class="gallery-card-tag">Ch.4 · Convolution</span>
</div>
</a>
</div>

<div class="gallery-card-body">
<div class="gallery-card-title">Why Linear Phase Matters</div>
<p class="gallery-card-desc">Two filters, the same magnitude response: the linear-phase FIR preserves a pulse's shape while the causal IIR smears its edges — the story is in the group delay.</p>
<span class="gallery-card-tag">Ch.6 · FIR vs IIR</span>

<div class="gallery-card">
<a href="gallery/decimation_alias.qmd">
<img class="gallery-card-img" src="Figure/figure_decimation_alias.png" alt="Anti-alias filtering before decimation">
<div class="gallery-card-body">
<div class="gallery-card-title">Downsampling Needs a Filter</div>
<p class="gallery-card-desc">Keep every 5th sample and a 700 Hz tone folds to a phantom 100 Hz. Low-pass first — the anti-alias filter — and it vanishes cleanly. You can't un-fold an alias.</p>
<span class="gallery-card-tag">Ch.6 · Decimation</span>
</div>
</a>
</div>
